story: projmap builds one page that explains a repository to someone new: its words, parts, rules, decisions and issues.
The tool gathers live facts itself: issues and pull requests through gh, modules and their imports, and the files each pull request changed.
People, helped by a Claude skill, write short records in content.json, and every field has a word cap.
A drift check compares the two, so the page says when the records are behind the repo.
The page is served locally, built as one HTML file, published by a CI template, or summarised in a Claude Code pane.

terms.plain: One short hand-written entry in content.json, such as a term, a component or a decision.
terms.example: A decision record has what, why and cost.

terms.plain: Something the tool gathers itself each build and nobody writes by hand.
terms.example: An issue's stage, or the modules a pull request touched.

terms.plain: The most words a record's field may hold; build and check fail when one is over.
terms.example: A component's does field holds at most 25 words.

terms.plain: An ID in the repo with no record on the map, or a record whose ID is gone.
terms.example: An open issue with no line in content.json.

terms.plain: The folder holding projmap.json and content.json, found in .projmap, docs/map or docs/projmap.
terms.example: This repo keeps its map in .projmap.

terms.plain: Where an issue stands, picked as the first stage whose conditions hold.
terms.example: In review, when a pull request for it is open.

terms.plain: The modules an issue changes, read from its pull requests, or predicted from its text when it has none.
terms.example: Pull request 4 touched the tool module.

components.name: Tool
components.does: Gathers live facts, joins them with content.json, checks caps and drift, and serves or writes the page.
components.takes: projmap.json, content.json, gh, the source tree
components.gives: the page, check results, facts and summary JSON

components.name: Page
components.does: One self-contained HTML file that draws every view from the data the tool embeds in it.

components.name: Skill
components.does: Tells Claude how to set up or refresh content.json and propose the change as a pull request.

components.name: Pane
components.does: A Claude Code mod that runs projmap summary and shows open issues beside the chat.

components.name: CI template
components.does: A GitHub Actions workflow that rebuilds the page on issue and pull request changes and publishes it privately.
components.takes: the default branch and GitHub events
components.gives: the page on Cloudflare Pages behind Access

links.how: The page reads the data keys the tool embeds, so renaming one breaks a view.
The pane parses projmap summary output, so changing its JSON shape breaks the pane.
The skill follows the commands and caps the tool defines; schema.md must match them.
The workflow installs the tool and runs build and check, so their flags must stay stable.

rules.name: Records stay short
rules.plain: Every record field has a word cap, and build and check refuse a map with a record over it.
rules.bad: A paragraph pasted into a term.

rules.name: The published page stays private
rules.plain: The CI template refuses to publish unless the address sends visitors to Cloudflare Access.
rules.ok: Publishing after Access is set up.
rules.bad: Publishing to an open pages.dev address.

rules.name: Records come from the repo
rules.plain: Every record traces to a file, issue or pull request; the skill leaves a record out rather than guess.
rules.ok: A decision copied from a workflow comment.

decisions.what: Every record field has a word cap.
decisions.why: So the page cannot grow into another long document.
decisions.cost: Build fails until an over-long record is cut down.

decisions.what: The tool never writes records; the skill proposes them as a pull request.
decisions.why: A person approves knowledge, and CI uses no Claude usage.
decisions.cost: The map lags behind until someone merges a refresh; the drift check says so meanwhile.

decisions.what: The workflow runs on pull_request_target and never checks out pull request code.
decisions.why: A pull request cannot change what runs next to the Cloudflare token.
decisions.cost: The page is always built from the default branch, not from the pull request.

decisions.what: No concurrency group; each run waits, then stops if a newer run exists.
decisions.why: A concurrency group cancels earlier runs, and those show as failures.
decisions.cost: Every run waits 20 seconds before building.

decisions.what: Publishing stops unless the address redirects to Cloudflare Access.
decisions.why: The page is private, and an open address must never receive it.
decisions.cost: Access must be set up before the first publish.

commands.plain: Add a map folder to the repo you are in.
Serve the page on localhost:4400 and rebuild it as things change.
Write the page as one HTML file.
List drift and over-long records; exits 1 if there are any.
Print the live facts as JSON, for whoever writes the records.
Print a short JSON summary, which the pane reads.
